questions.q: What is Azure Monitor, and how does it start collecting data?
options: Azure's platform-wide observability service, which collects data from almost every resource automatically
A billing tool that has nothing to do with performance or health data
A service that requires a separate agent to be manually installed on every single resource before any data is collected
A storage-only service with no relationship to monitoring
questions.explain: Azure Monitor collects basic data from nearly every Azure resource automatically, without requiring a separate monitoring agent to be configured first.

questions.q: What is a "metric" in Azure Monitor, and what is it good for?
options: A numerical value collected at regular intervals, like CPU percentage — good for watching a number change over time
A detailed, timestamped record of a single event
A rule that automatically deletes underperforming resources
A billing statement summarizing monthly charges
questions.explain: Metrics are numbers tracked over time, which makes them useful for spotting trends like rising CPU usage.

questions.q: What is a "log" in Azure Monitor, and how is it different from a metric?
options: A detailed, timestamped record of an event — richer than a single number, good for investigating what actually happened
A log is identical to a metric with no meaningful difference
A log only stores billing information, never event details
Logs cannot be searched or investigated after they are recorded
questions.explain: Logs capture full event details (an error message, a request, an audit entry), which is richer information than a single tracked number.

questions.q: What does an "alert" do in Azure Monitor?
options: It watches metrics or logs and notifies you (or triggers an automated action) when a defined condition is met
It permanently deletes a resource once triggered
It only sends a notification once per year regardless of conditions
Alerts have no relationship to metrics or logs at all
questions.explain: Alerts are rules built on top of metrics or logs, such as CPU staying above 90% for five minutes, that notify or trigger an action when met.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Azure Monitor's value matters even before anything has broken?
options: Because collection starts automatically, the data is already there to answer questions later, instead of wishing you'd turned on monitoring after an incident
Azure Monitor only becomes useful after a resource has already failed
There is no value to monitoring until an outage actually occurs
Azure Monitor cannot collect any historical data, only real-time data
questions.explain: Because Azure Monitor collects automatically from the start, you have historical data available to investigate a question later, rather than having missed the window.
